newsitem.title: EGYPT: T-bill auctions push Egypt pound interbank up.
newsitem.headline: T-bill auctions push Egypt pound interbank up.

text.p: Overnight interbank rates on the Egyptian pound rose in a very short private-sector market on Tuesday to between 8-7/8 and 9-3/4 percent from Monday's range of 8-1/2 and 9-1/2 percent, bankers said.
"New issues of treasury bills are withdrawing liquidity from the market," one banker said.
The Central Bank has been auctioning for the past three weeks t-bills worth about 300 million pounds more than the total of maturing bills.
The latest offer on Monday was for 1.1 billion pounds in 91-day bills in Wednesday's auction, to replace bills worth 665.3 million maturing on Thursday.
Many bankers said they did not make one-week deals. Those who dealt quoted nine percent against Sunday's range of 7-3/4 and 8-1/2 percent. No banker did one-week deals on Monday.

Some bankers quoted public-sector banks on Tuesday at around 10 percent. Bankers have said that the banks had lowered their official minimum lending rate to around 9-1/2 percent from the longstanding rate of 10-1/2 percent. The new levels have not been officially announced.
